metadata.content:
That confirms exactly why runtime-locks was not where you were looking.
Runtime process PID 39374 is running with:
cwd:
/Users/erictouko/dev/korelumina/apps/lumina-runtime
And runtimeLock.ts builds the lock directory from:
TypeScriptconst LOCK_DIR = path.resolve(
  process.cwd(),
  "runtime-locks",
);
Therefore the actual lock location is:
/Users/erictouko/dev/korelumina/apps/lumina-runtime/runtime-locks
not
/Users/erictouko/dev/korelumina/runtime-locks
Check it:
Bashls -la apps/lumina-runtime/runtime-locks
or
Bashfind apps/lumina-runtime -name "*.lock"
Current findings:
Fixed


Runtime lock cleanup bug found.


removeRuntime() now releases locks.


Build passes.


Verified


Runtime supervisor running.


Runtime recovery running.


Runtime registry healthy.


Runtime can start and stop manually.


Runtime metrics show Elegance Sync running on port 4201.


New root cause discovered
This is now the bigger issue:
JSONGET /api/runtime/projects
{
  "ok": true,
  "projects": []
}
but
Bashcurl -H "x-korelumina-role: super_admin" \
http://localhost:4100/api/runtime/projects
returns all projects.
That means the runtime itself can see the projects.
The filtering layer is hiding them.
This aligns with earlier findings:


Workspace access system added during reconstruction.


canViewProject() filtering exists.


Dashboard empty.


Runtime project API empty unless super_admin header supplied.


The next investigation is no longer runtime locks.
The next investigation is:
Bashgrep -R "canViewProject" apps/lumina-runtime/src -n

grep -R "x-korelumina-role" apps/lumina-runtime/src -n

grep -R "listProjects()" apps/lumina-runtime/src/routes -n
We need to trace why normal requests are being filtered to zero projects while the super_admin request returns all seven projects. That is the most likely reason the Builder lost project visibility and subsequently lost runtime auto-start behavior.
